title: AACE Act
official_summary:
Accelerating Appraisals and Conservation Efforts Act or AACE Act

This act relaxes requirements for the Department of the Interior in appraising and valuing real property for transactions over which Interior has jurisdiction.

Specifically, a private real property appraiser needs only to be licensed or certified in one state to perform appraisal or valuation services for real property over which Interior has jurisdiction. Currently, if a private assessor is used for a real property transaction within Interior's jurisdiction, that assessor must be licensed or certified in the state where that transaction occurs. 

When using private appraisers, Interior shall, to the maximum extent practicable, use private appraisers who are certified general real property appraisers licensed in the state where the transaction occurs.

Additionally, Interior may use a private appraiser who is licensed outside the state in which the transaction occurs only if private appraisers licensed in that state are unavailable, not assignment qualified, or not cost competitive. Interior must make the text of all policies related to such appraisals public.

summary.headline: New law lets the Interior Department use private property appraisers licensed in any state, not just the state where the land is.
summary.what_it_does: The law lets the Department of the Interior hire private appraisers who are licensed or certified in at least one state to value land and other real property it handles. Before, the appraiser had to be licensed in the state where the deal took place. Interior must still prefer appraisers licensed in the local state when it can, and may use out-of-state appraisers only if local ones are unavailable, not qualified for the job, or cost too much. Interior must also make its appraisal policies public.

who_it_affects.how: Appraisers licensed in one state may now be hired for Interior property deals in other states when local appraisers are unavailable, not qualified, or more costly.

who_it_affects.group: Landowners and others in property deals with the Interior Department
who_it_affects.how: Their property may be valued by an appraiser licensed outside their state in some cases.
It has more options for hiring appraisers and must publish the text of its appraisal policies.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 4, 2025; the summary does not give a separate start date.
